title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 6.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 6, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Solomon spoke about the LORD dwelling in darkness
David had a desire to build a house
The ark was placed in the house
questions.correctAnswer: Solomon spoke about the LORD dwelling in darkness
questions.explanation: This is the first mention in the chapter where Solomon speaks about the LORD in 2 Chronicles 6:1.

questions.question: What did Solomon say he had built for the LORD?
questions.explanation: Solomon states in 2 Chronicles 6:2 that he has built a house of habitation for the LORD.

questions.question: Who did Solomon bless after turning his face?
questions.explanation: In 2 Chronicles 6:3, Solomon blessed the whole congregation of Israel.

questions.question: What did Solomon say about the LORD God of Israel?
options: He is like no other god
He fulfilled what He spoke to David
questions.correctAnswer: He fulfilled what He spoke to David
questions.explanation: Solomon mentions in 2 Chronicles 6:4 that the LORD God of Israel has fulfilled that which He spoke with His mouth to David.

questions.question: Which city did the LORD choose for His name to be?
questions.explanation: According to 2 Chronicles 6:6, the LORD chose Jerusalem for His name.

questions.question: What was in the heart of David concerning the house?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 6:7 states that it was in the heart of David to build a house for the name of the LORD.

questions.question: Who did the LORD say would build the house?
questions.explanation: The LORD told David in 2 Chronicles 6:9 that his son, who would come forth from him, would build the house.

questions.question: What has the LORD performed according to Solomon?
questions.explanation: In 2 Chronicles 6:10, Solomon states that the LORD has performed His word that He spoke.

questions.question: What did Solomon put in the house?
questions.explanation: According to 2 Chronicles 6:11, Solomon put the ark in the house, which contains the covenant of the LORD.

questions.question: What did Solomon do before the altar of the LORD?
options: He stood and spread forth his hands
questions.correctAnswer: He stood and spread forth his hands
questions.explanation: In 2 Chronicles 6:12, Solomon stood before the altar and spread forth his hands in the presence of the congregation.

questions.question: How did Solomon describe the LORD God of Israel?
questions.explanation: In 2 Chronicles 6:14, Solomon describes the LORD God of Israel as one who keeps covenant and shows mercy.

questions.question: Is it true that Solomon built a house for the name of the LORD?
questions.explanation: Solomon indeed states that he built a house for the name of the LORD in 2 Chronicles 6:2.

questions.question: Did the LORD tell David that he did well to want to build a house?
questions.explanation: The LORD acknowledged in 2 Chronicles 6:8 that it was well that it was in David's heart to build a house.

questions.question: The ark contained the books of the law.
questions.explanation: The text in 2 Chronicles 6:11 states that the ark contains the covenant, not the books of the law.

questions.question: Solomon prayed silently before the altar of the LORD.
questions.explanation: According to 2 Chronicles 6:12, Solomon stood and spread forth his hands before the altar, indicating he did not pray silently.

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What has God done with His servant David according to 2 Chronicles 6:15?
questions.explanation: God has kept with His servant David that which He has promised him, as stated in 2 Chronicles 6:15.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 6:16 promise will happen if David's children take heed to their way?
options: They shall sit on the throne
questions.correctAnswer: They shall sit on the throne
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 6:16 states that if David's children take heed to their way, a man will not fail to sit on the throne of Israel.

questions.question: What is Solomon asking God to verify in 2 Chronicles 6:17?
questions.explanation: Solomon is asking the Lord to let His word be verified, which He has spoken to His servant David, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 6:17.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 6:18, what is the significance of the house Solomon built?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 6:18 highlights that even heaven cannot contain God, much less the house Solomon built, indicating that God cannot truly dwell with men.

questions.question: What does Solomon request God to have respect for in 2 Chronicles 6:19?
questions.explanation: In 2 Chronicles 6:19, Solomon asks God to have respect for the prayer of His servant and to hearken to his supplication.

questions.question: What condition is mentioned in 2 Chronicles 6:24 for God to forgive His people?
options: They must return and confess His name
questions.correctAnswer: They must return and confess His name
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 6:24 states that if His people return and confess His name, God will hear from heaven and forgive their sin.

questions.question: What does Solomon ask God to do when there is no rain in 2 Chronicles 6:26?
questions.explanation: In 2 Chronicles 6:26, Solomon asks God to hear from heaven and forgive the sin of His servants when they pray for rain during drought.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 6:27 indicate about God's response to His people's prayer?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 6:27 assures that God will forgive the sins of His servants and send rain upon the land when they pray sincerely.

questions.question: What does Solomon acknowledge about the covenant in 2 Chronicles 6:14?
questions.explanation: In 2 Chronicles 6:14, Solomon acknowledges that there is no God like the LORD who keeps covenant, affirming the reliability of God's promises.

questions.question: What does Solomon emphasize about God in 2 Chronicles 6:2?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 6:2 shows Solomon's recognition that God has chosen to dwell among His people and desires a place for His habitation.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 6:21, how should the people of Israel approach God?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 6:21 instructs that the people should make supplications toward the house and expect God to hear them.

questions.question: What does God promise in 2 Chronicles 6:23 regarding justice?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 6:23 states that God will judge His servants by requiting the wicked and justifying the righteous according to their actions.

questions.question: Will God hear prayers made toward the house built by Solomon according to 2 Chronicles 6:20?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 6:20 indicates that God's eyes will be open upon the house, and He will hear prayers made towards it.

questions.question: Is it true that Solomon built the house for God because God commanded him to according to 2 Chronicles 6:10?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 6:9 clarifies that although it was in David's heart to build the house, it was actually Solomon who built it according to God's direction.

questions.question: Does 2 Chronicles 6:28 suggest that God will not respond to any situation His people face?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 6:28 does not suggest that God will not respond; rather, it implies that He will hear and act upon their prayers in times of trouble.

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 6.

questions.question: What should every man or all of Israel do when they know their own sore and grief?
options: Spread forth their hands in this house
questions.correctAnswer: Spread forth their hands in this house
questions.explanation: This is stated in 2 Chronicles 6:29, which emphasizes the action of spreading forth hands in the house of the Lord as a form of prayer and supplication.

questions.question: From where should God hear the prayers made in His house?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 6:30 specifies that God should hear from heaven, indicating His divine dwelling place.

questions.question: What does God know according to 2 Chronicles 6:30?
options: The hearts of the children of men
questions.correctAnswer: The hearts of the children of men
questions.explanation: The verse 2 Chronicles 6:30 mentions that God alone knows the hearts of the children of men, emphasizing His omniscience.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the prayers made by the stranger according to 2 Chronicles 6:33?
options: To know God's name and fear Him
questions.correctAnswer: To know God's name and fear Him
questions.explanation: In 2 Chronicles 6:33, it states that the prayers of the stranger are meant for all people to know God's name and fear Him, demonstrating inclusivity in worship.

questions.question: What should the Israelites do if they are carried away captives to a foreign land?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 6:38 instructs that if they return to God with all their heart in captivity, they should pray toward their land, indicating the importance of remembering their heritage.

questions.question: What does Solomon ask God to do regarding His eyes and ears in 2 Chronicles 6:40?
options: Close them to the sins of Israel
Open them to the prayer made in this place
Turn them away from this house
Ignore the prayers of the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: Open them to the prayer made in this place
questions.explanation: In 2 Chronicles 6:40, Solomon beseeches God to open His eyes and ears to the prayers made in the newly built temple, signifying its importance.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'sore' (חֳלִי) in 2 Chronicles 6:29 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'חֳלִי' (sore) in this context refers to a state of sickness or affliction, which the individuals are aware of in their prayers.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used in 2 Chronicles 6:39 when it mentions 'hear thou from the heavens'?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'hear thou from the heavens' employs repetition to emphasize the call for God's attention to the prayers of His people.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of God's willingness to hear prayer in times of distress as seen in 2 Chronicles 6:34?
questions.explanation: Psalm 34:17 echoes the theme in 2 Chronicles 6:34 where it states that the Lord hears the cries of the righteous in distress.

questions.question: Which passage in the New Testament reflects the theme of forgiveness found in 2 Chronicles 6:39?
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:14 discusses the importance of forgiveness, mirroring the theme of seeking forgiveness in 2 Chronicles 6:39.

questions.question: What comes immediately before 2 Chronicles 6:30?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 6:30 follows the acknowledgment of human sin in verse 29, highlighting the need for divine forgiveness.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 6:36, what is stated about man and sin?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 6:36 clearly states that there is no man who does not sin, acknowledging the universal nature of sin among humanity.

questions.question: The statement 'Thou only knowest the hearts of the children of men' signifies what about God's nature in 2 Chronicles 6:30?
questions.explanation: This statement highlights God's omniscience, as expressed in 2 Chronicles 6:30, where He alone knows the hearts of men.

questions.question: True or False: Solomon built the temple according to 2 Chronicles 6:10.
questions.explanation: This is true as 2 Chronicles 6:10 indicates that Solomon built the house for the name of the Lord God of Israel.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Chronicles 6:42 mentions God's promise to David regarding his anointed.
questions.explanation: This is false; 2 Chronicles 6:42 does mention God's mercies for David but focuses on not turning away from His anointed, without a promise context.

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 6:1 teach about God's nature?
options: God is visible to all men
God is limited to the temple alone
God does not communicate with humans
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 6:1 states that 'The LORD hath said that he would dwell in the thick darkness,' teaching the doctrine that God's presence is mysterious and transcendent, beyond human sight.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine election and covenant is taught in 2 Chronicles 6:6?
options: God chose Jerusalem and David for His name to dwell there
God randomly selected Israel's rulers without purpose
God's presence is equally in all cities without distinction
God does not establish earthly dynasties
questions.correctAnswer: God chose Jerusalem and David for His name to dwell there
questions.explanation: Verse 6 teaches the doctrine of divine election by showing God choosing Jerusalem and David specifically for His name and covenant presence, emphasizing God's purposeful selection.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's faithfulness to His promises is taught in 2 Chronicles 6:10?
options: God faithfully fulfills His promises to David through Solomon
God often breaks His promises to human leaders
God's promises are conditional on human perfection
God's promises are symbolic and not literal
questions.correctAnswer: God faithfully fulfills His promises to David through Solomon
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 6:10 states that 'The LORD therefore hath performed his word that he hath spoken,' underscoring the doctrine of God's faithfulness in fulfilling covenant promises.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 6:14 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Verse 14 declares that God 'keepest covenant, and shewest mercy unto thy servants,' highlighting His attribute of covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in 2 Chronicles 6:30?
questions.explanation: Verse 30 says 'for thou only knowest the hearts of the children of men,' demonstrating God's omniscience—His complete knowledge of human hearts.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 6:11–12 connect to the broader biblical theme of God's covenant presence?
options: By placing the ark with the covenant in the temple, it fulfills God's promise to dwell among His people
By establishing a new covenant unrelated to the past
By rejecting the ark as a symbol of God's presence
By emphasizing human merit over divine promise
questions.correctAnswer: By placing the ark with the covenant in the temple, it fulfills God's promise to dwell among His people
questions.explanation: Verses 11 and 12 show Solomon placing the ark of the covenant in the temple, symbolizing God's fulfilled promise to be present with Israel, a central biblical redemptive theme.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 6:18 anticipate New Testament teachings about God's transcendence and immanence?
options: By acknowledging God's transcendence beyond the temple but still requesting His presence
By teaching that God is confined to the temple alone
By denying God's presence in heaven
By suggesting God is indifferent to human worship
questions.correctAnswer: By acknowledging God's transcendence beyond the temple but still requesting His presence
questions.explanation: Verse 18 states that even the heavens cannot contain God, yet Solomon seeks His presence, prefiguring the New Testament understanding of God's transcendent yet immanent nature.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 6:24 and 6:25 teach about repentance and restoration?
options: Confession and prayer lead to divine forgiveness and restoration to the land
Repentance has no effect on divine judgment
Restoration is solely based on military success
questions.correctAnswer: Confession and prayer lead to divine forgiveness and restoration to the land
questions.explanation: Verses 24 and 25 teach that when Israel confesses and prays in the temple, God hears and forgives, restoring them to their land, demonstrating the doctrine of repentance and covenant restoration.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 6:26 and 6:27 teach about God's discipline and provision?
options: God disciplines withhold rain but restores it upon sincere prayer and repentance
God's discipline is final and irrevocable
Provision is independent of human repentance
Rain is a random natural occurrence unrelated to divine will
questions.correctAnswer: God disciplines withhold rain but restores it upon sincere prayer and repentance
questions.explanation: Verses 26 and 27 describe drought as discipline for sin but promise rain when the people repent and pray, teaching God's disciplinary justice and merciful provision.

questions.question: What combined doctrine is taught by 2 Chronicles 6:32 and 6:33 concerning Gentiles and salvation?
options: Gentiles who come to pray in God's house are heard, revealing God's universal concern
Salvation is exclusive to Israel only
Gentiles cannot access God's presence through prayer
The temple is only for Israelite rituals, excluding foreigners
questions.correctAnswer: Gentiles who come to pray in God's house are heard, revealing God's universal concern
questions.explanation: Verses 32 and 33 teach that strangers who come from afar and pray are heard by God, showing His inclusive mercy and foreshadowing the universal scope of salvation.

questions.question: Sceptics claim 2 Chronicles 6:18-20 teaches that God is confined to a physical temple. What does this passage actually teach?
options: God transcends heaven and earth but chooses to hear prayer in the temple
God is limited to the temple's physical space
The temple is merely symbolic with no real divine presence
God does not hear prayers made in the temple
questions.correctAnswer: God transcends heaven and earth but chooses to hear prayer in the temple
questions.explanation: Verses 18-20 clarify that although heaven cannot contain God, He regards the temple as a special place to hear prayers, demonstrating divine transcendence coupled with condescension.

questions.question: What doctrine about the role of the king is taught in 2 Chronicles 6:16?
options: The king's dynasty depends on obedience to God's law
The king rules by human wisdom alone
The king's reign is unconditional regardless of conduct
The king is a divine being
questions.correctAnswer: The king's dynasty depends on obedience to God's law
questions.explanation: Verse 16 links the continuation of David's line on the throne to his children's obedience to God's law, teaching conditional covenant kingship.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is especially highlighted in 2 Chronicles 6:42?
questions.explanation: Verse 42 appeals to God to 'remember the mercies of David,' emphasizing God's attribute of mercy toward His anointed.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 6:34-35 contribute to the theme of divine guidance in warfare within redemptive history?
options: God hears and maintains the cause of His people when they pray toward the chosen city in war
Victory in war depends solely on military might
God is indifferent to Israel's battles
Prayer has no effect on war outcomes
questions.correctAnswer: God hears and maintains the cause of His people when they pray toward the chosen city in war
questions.explanation: These verses teach that God's guidance and support in war are linked to prayer toward Jerusalem, affirming divine providence in historical conflicts.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 6:36-39 teach about exile, repentance, and restoration?
options: Exiled people who repent with all their heart are forgiven and restored by God
Exile is permanent and without hope of return
Repentance in exile is unnecessary for restoration
Restoration is based on political alliances only
questions.correctAnswer: Exiled people who repent with all their heart are forgiven and restored by God
questions.explanation: These verses affirm that even in captivity, genuine repentance toward God and the temple leads to divine forgiveness and restoration, highlighting God's redemptive mercy.
